name: Ahimaaz
overview: Ahimaaz was a male figure known primarily as one of King Solomon's twelve deputies, serving in the region of Naphtali. His role as a deputy highlights his administrative importance during Solomon's reign. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahimaaz means '[my] brother is fury,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name. This meaning is noted in the scriptural reference 1 Kings 4:15. There are no titles or additional names associated with him.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Ahimaaz was the husband of Basemath, as noted in 1 Kings 4:15. Beyond this marital relationship, no further family connections are documented in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Ahimaaz's significance lies in his administrative role under King Solomon, where he was entrusted as one of twelve deputies overseeing the kingdom's governance. His assignment to Naphtali indicates responsibility for this northern territory, reflecting Solomon's organized and divinely guided rule. This position underscores the orderly government established during Solomon's reign, in which Ahimaaz played a part.
